attributes.source: NatCen Patterns of Play, Account Data Stage Report, 2018–19: 78.4% male among betting-active accounts with gender recorded; binary survey crosswalk assumed. PMC9757982 Table of winter activities supplies sex-specific prior play in init.
NatCen Patterns of Play: 53.9% under 35; within/beyond this band assumed. Spin sizes £1.05/£1.30: DCMS Consultation on a maximum stake limit for online slots, 2018–19 account data.

NatCen Patterns of Play football 77.1%, horse racing 68.0%, broad 6.4%. Assumed allocation matching these overlapping margins; broad group uses both. Racing-only proxy not the 30.8% mainly racing figure conditional on >200 betting days. Weights assumed.
NatCen Patterns of Play annual betting turnover / 12: median £7.50, mean £170.75. Assumed discrete distribution with heavy upper tail and small independent jitter; not fitted to pandemic outcomes.

PMC9757982: unweighted job loss 3.96%; furlough 7.8/11.5%, continued employment 63.1/60.1% men/women. Assumed disjoint risk ordering; remaining survey statuses pooled. Rank is fixed for counterfactuals.

sketch: Two or three sentences about one adult online sports-account holder who bet at least once last winter. Describe their familiar sporting ritual, an ordinary demand on their time or budget, and whether unfamiliar games appeal; match their age, stake band, interest and curiosity. Do not infer a job from turnover, assign an occupation inconsistent with unspecified employment, invent product history, or mention future events, closures, offers, countries or years.
